text.text_excerpt: The only thing I love more than beer is making my own beer. I've been doing it off and on since 2005, usually making one or two batches then unfortunately putting my equipment aside for a while, sometimes a year or more for various reasons. But every time I dust off my stuff and decide to make a batch I go to Brewstock to get my supplies. In fact, I bought all of my equipment here. The owner, Aaron, is one of the nicest and most knowledgeable people in the homebrew community I've ever met. I can go in there with an idea for a recipe and he can help me craft exactly what I want. Want to do a lager but don't have the climate control to keep it chilled during fermentation? Aaron can provide ...

I cannot say enough good things about this place and its staff. They have everything you need to start brewing and they are more than willing to teach you anything you need to know and answer any questions you may have. You can literally walk in here knowing absolutely NOTHING about brewing beer and walk out ten minutes later with EVERYTHING you need to start your first batch that night. Just tell them what you like and they will tell you how to make it. Another great thing about this place is that they keep records of your purchases, so if you can't remember the recipe you made three weeks ago, they can tell you, then they will go through the store and collect everything you need.

Aaron, the owner, is the most knowledgeable brewmaster you could ever hope to meet. I am making the leap from intermediate to more advanced brewing, and Aaron helped me every step. This place has an excellent selection of hops and grains, and all of the supplies that you might need. I custom made a pale ale brew based off of Aarons guidance. I have been to an abundance of brewery stores and nothing comes close to this place. They have everything you need, and the knowledge to put it to use. If you are serious about your beer, you need to shop here. That rhyme was completely unintentional.
